Continued - THE STRONG MEN WE ARE RAISING

Yesterday’s post sparked quite a few reactions.

And I think one thing needs to be made clear:

This is not an argument against change.

It was never about saying the younger generation is doomed.

If anything, it was meant to make us look beyond the trend, understand the psychology behind it, and question the kind of future we are collectively building.

Let me take it a step further.

I remember being on another space where people were projecting what the next generation would become.

Some said they were genuinely scared.

That the next generation would be worse.
Less disciplined.
Less responsible.
Less connected to reality.
But I remember thinking:

Haven’t people said the same thing about every generation?

I vividly remember my parents talking about their generation with a certain dignity and telling us how different and sometimes disappointing they feared ours would become.

Yet look at what our generation has produced.

Nigeria has produced people who have built companies, technologies and institutions that operate far beyond our borders:

Shola Akinlade & Ezra Olubi built Paystack, which Stripe acquired for more than $200 million.

Iyinoluwa Aboyeji co-founded Andela and Flutterwave and has continued investing in Africa’s next generation of founders.

Olugbenga “GB” Agboola helped build Flutterwave into one of Africa’s most significant payment companies.

Odunayo Eweniyi, alongside her PiggyVest co-founders, helped build one of Nigeria’s most influential savings and investment platforms.

And this isn’t limited to fintech.
We have Nigerian engineers, creators, designers, founders, artists, researchers and builders solving problems that previous generations couldn’t even imagine.

We have young Nigerians building in:

AI
Blockchain
Fintech
Software
Media
Entertainment
Fashion
Education
Creative technology

And even among the younger generation, there are already people proving that the story isn’t simply one of decline.
There are young developers teaching other teenagers to code, young entrepreneurs building businesses, and young Nigerians creating communities around technology and innovation.

So yes, I agree with the “OLODO uprising.”

But I also believe in something else:

THE GENIUS UPRISING.

The builders.

The thinkers.

The disciplined.

The curious.

The ones who understand that going viral is not the same thing as building value.

The ones who understand that money is not the same thing as wealth.

The ones who understand that freedom without responsibility is not progress.

And this is where the conversation becomes personal.

Because the real question isn’t:

“What is wrong with Gen Z?”

The real question is:

“What kind of next generation are YOU raising?”

Because somewhere in the future, your children will become someone else’s leaders.

They will become:

Founders.
Engineers.
Doctors.
Investors.
Policymakers.
Teachers.
Creators.
Parents.
Builders.

And I want to raise children who can look at the world they inherited and say:

“Our parents didn’t fail us.”

I want to raise children who are evidence that despite everything happening around us, we still understood the assignment.

Children who can embrace technology without becoming slaves to it.

Children who can enjoy freedom without abandoning responsibility.

Children who can understand modernity without despising their heritage.

Children who can pursue wealth without losing their values.

Children who can be ambitious without becoming entitled.

Children who can question the world without losing the ability to think.

Because the future isn’t automatically going to be better.

We have to build the people capable of making it better.

And that brings us back to the cycle:

Hard times create strong men. Strong men create good times. Good times create weak men. And weak men create hard times.

Yesterday, I was talking about the cycle.

Today, I’m asking you to look in the mirror.

Are you raising the generation that will break the cycle or continue it?

Because perhaps the future isn’t determined by what Gen Z becomes.

Perhaps it is determined by what we choose to raise.
And that is a much more personal question.

I'm shocked most people use an Android phone like it's still 2014.

Here are 10 Android hacks that'll make your phone feel like it secretly got promoted.

---

1. Circle to Search lets you search whatever is on your screen without doing the sacred ritual of opening 17 apps.

---

2. Circle an image, product, place, or text and Google basically goes, "Yep, I know that thing."

---

3. Use AI features for photo editing, rewriting, summaries, translation, transcription, and pretending manual work never existed.

---

4. Automate routines so your phone changes settings by itself instead of waiting for its human manager.

---

5. Make WiFi, battery saver, silent mode, and apps trigger automatically because tapping buttons is apparently a full-time job.

---

6. Turn on Adaptive Battery and limit background apps so your battery stops disappearing like your weekend.

---

7. Dark mode can also help reduce power consumption on phones with OLED displays while making everything look 73% cooler.

---

8. Unlock Developer Options by tapping Build Number seven times, which sounds suspiciously like entering a cheat code.

---

9. Developer Options give you access to animation tweaks, debugging tools, and advanced controls your grandma definitely shouldn't touch.

---

10. Review camera, microphone, location, and app permissions because your calculator probably doesn't need to know where you had lunch.

---

11. Split Screen lets you watch something while taking notes, bringing desktop-level procrastination straight to your pocket.

---

12. Research and write side by side instead of switching apps every six seconds and forgetting why you switched.

---

13. Check Notification History to find that notification you accidentally swiped away at Formula 1 speed.

---

14. Use priority alerts and silent notifications so your phone stops screaming about every discount, meme, and app update.

---

15. Enable Find My Device because "I'll never lose my phone" is famous last-words material.

---

16. Theft Detection Lock can help protect your phone when someone decides your Android should become their Android.

---

17. Offline Lock adds protection even when your phone loses connectivity, because thieves aren't always generous with WiFi.

---

18. Keep security updates installed because "Update later" should not become a five-year personal philosophy.

---

19. Learn gestures for screenshots, one-handed mode, Quick Tap, camera launching, and other tiny shortcuts that save ridiculous amounts of tapping.

---

20. Customize Quick Settings so the controls you actually use are available before your thumb files a workplace complaint.

I've been working on this little notch app that has a few keyboard shortcuts.  I wanted to use established UI patterns to teach the user about those shortcuts w/o cluttering the UI, so...

1. I asked codex, something like:

"help me find a standard UI pattern to expose shortcuts to the user in a way that doesn't clutter the UI. try using image gen to generate a mockup first."

It responded with something like image 2.

2. I highlighted the suggested interaction convention text and clicked "more details"

This is magic.  What happens:

FIRST: codex app sends that annotation along with some context from your ongoing work thread to chat gpt (doesn't use you codex limits!). This opens the thread in a "quick chat" window with the context primed.

SECOND: I follow up with a new message like:

[pasted screenshot of the current UI]
"can you do research on this UI convention?"

It goes out to the web, discovers a bunch of sources on UI/UX patterns relevant to showing shortcuts to a user in a macOS app.  Gives me a crash course on the topic. Very cool.

THIRD: I then follow up with: "generate a mockup illustrating your suggested pattern(s)"

It then generates an image doing just that (image 3)

3. I click the "Add to Chat" button in the quick chat window header (image 4)

This little button re-injects the context from this quick chat thread (including the mockup image) back into the main Codex work thread (wtf!)

LAST: I follow up, back in the main chat now:

[Shortcut Discovery Design thread] review both suggested approaches (your own against the helper research thread) and decide on a best final approach.

This results in a final interaction pattern suggestion where it drops its own "hover-only keyboard icon" and in adopts portions of the external thread's researched pattern.

Then I follow up with "mockup pls"...

This Paper is one of the cleverest solutions I’ve seen for fixing Diffusion Alignment.

If you’ve worked with RLHF or Reward Backprop on DiTs, you must be tired of delayed feedback. 

Evaluating only the final image makes credit assignment a total nightmare. 

You either run out of VRAM trying to unroll the full trajectory, or you fight insane gradient variance with online RL.

The authors solve this by sticking learnable, position-free "register tokens" into a frozen DiT. 

Instead of waiting until step 50, these registers pull dense reward signals directly out of noisy intermediate latents. 

It turns out you can accurately judge trajectory quality surprisingly early in the denoising process.

What makes this paper stand out is how practical the applications are:

1-For training: Their distillation setup (RG-OPD) skips standard policy gradients entirely and hits the same alignment performance while using up to 33x fewer GPU hours. That’s huge for making alignment accessible.

2-For inference: You can use their Reward-Guided Sampling (RGS) to steer generation live off these register gradients thus improving both prompt adherence and visual quality without retraining or touching model weights.

It’s a super clean, well thought-out approach that addresses both the compute bottleneck and inference control at once. 

Definitely worth a read if you're working on generative models:
https://t.co/tfkSPmYwiU
